I don't have any notes for you yet. None of my searches or page reads worked, so I haven't read a single source on Mark 14:1–24.

**What happened:**
- I tried to open the Enduring Word commentary on Mark 14 directly. The tool refused because it only opens pages that first turn up in a search result.
- My first batch of searches crashed. The search results came back in a different form than my code expected, so nothing was saved or shown.
- When I tried again, I'd hit the limit on tool calls for this turn, and the other tools I have can't reach the internet.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to leave out anything I couldn't find, so I haven't written any notes from memory.

**What I'll do next time, if you ask me to continue:**
1. **Verse-by-verse reading:** search for and read Enduring Word (Mark 14), Bible Hub's Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages for each verse, Precept Austin on Mark 14, and Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu).
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mainly vv. 22–24 ("this is My body", "blood of the covenant"):
   - Lutheran: LCMS and 1517 on Christ's real presence in the bread and wine.
   - Reformed: Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition on Christ's spiritual presence.
   - Baptist: Desiring God, GTY and Spurgeon on the Supper as a memorial.
   - Methodist: Seedbed and Wesley.
   - Pentecostal: AG.org and Enduring Word.
   - I'll also look for differences on v. 7 ("the poor you will always have") and v. 21 (betrayal and God's plan).
3. **Other views:**
   - Catholic and Orthodox (New Advent, Catholic.com, OCA) on transubstantiation, the Eucharist as sacrifice, and who the woman in v. 3 was.
   - NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey on the dating of the Passover in v. 12 and the 300 denarii in v. 5.
   - Any popular modern teaching on these verses that the allowed sites discuss.

Each point will have its page URL.
